title: The Cenozoic East Rhodopean Low‐Sulfidation Gold‐Silver Metallogenic Province, SE Bulgaria—Synthesis of Existing Data: A Review
content: The low-sulfidation silver-gold prospects in the Eastern Rhodope Mountains, SE Bulgaria, united in the East Rhodopean low-sulfidation gold-silver metallogenic province, contain a considerable precious-metal endowment for current and future mining. For the most promising prospects, geochronological, stratigraphical, biostratigraphical, structural, mineralogical, and stable-isotope data exist, but their origin remains not fully understood. In this paper, we review existing data on geodynamics, metamorphism, magmatism, and their geochronology in the Rhodope Crystalline Massif, as well as data on the geology, mineralogy, stable isotope geochemistry, and formation conditions of low-sulfidation gold deposits from the Eastern Rhodopes, SE Bulgaria. The aim is to provide a synopsis of the existing data to help one construct a new genetic model for this class of economic deposits. The main conclusions which can be drawn from the reviewed literature are the following: (i) geochronological and stratigraphic constraints clearly revealed older age of these de-posits than the local Late Eocene- Early Oligocene magmatism; (ii) there is isotop-ic evi-dence of meteoric origin of the fluids; (iii) there is a seismological evidence of slab rollback since Eocene to Late Miocene-Pliocene in the Rhodope realm, (iv) conveying role of the deeply penetrating detachment fault systems for hot uprising fluids is evidenced by hy-drothermal alteration and silicification, both strong in places; and (v) heating of mete-oric water in the area of high heat flux produced by the Cenozoic crustal extension and as-thenospheric mantle upwelling in the Eastern Rhodopes is seems to be a necessary condi-tion for the formation of these deposits.
